articles.title: From ‘nappies at the ballpark’ to the MLB: how Australia’s Travis Bazzana made baseball’s big league
articles.summary: The 24-year-old has taken his attention to detail from lining up bats and helmets as a toddler to helping the Cleveland Guardians towards the playoffs. When Sydney’s Travis Bazzana made his debut in Major League Baseball on 28 April, it was the culmination of a journey that began when he was a…
body: “From the time he could stand, Travis was always wanting to throw or hit balls with any type of bat or racket available,” says Travis’s mother, Jenny. “Any visitors to the house, including his grandparents, were immediately invited to play or compete with him.”

Travis transformed his eagerness into a passionate discipline that enabled him to become the first Australian top selection in MLB’s amateur draft and the Cleveland Guardians’ All-Star second baseman.

“He’s an animal,” Guardians pitcher Parker Messick told the Cleveland Plain Dealer. “He loves the game of baseball. He takes it very serious every at-bat. Every time he’s on first base, every play in the infield, he’s locked in.”

Despite being a rookie, the 24-year-old has excelled in the Guardians’ late surge for a spot in the MLB playoffs. In September, when Cleveland won seven of 10 games, Travis’s five home runs and safe hitting have helped put them into a strong position in the American League Central division alongside the Chicago White Sox.

articles.title: 'You have to start somewhere' - inexperienced GB team bid for Davis Cup Finals
articles.summary: Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line.
body: British number two Norrie felt pain in his arm during a practice session and will be replaced in Saturday's singles by world number 95 Toby Samuel.
"He wasn't able to accelerate on the ball like he wanted to," Davis Cup captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport.
"It's nothing major, but there's still a lot of tennis to be played this year and with that in mind, we had to make the difficult decision to replace him."
Great Britain have not reached the knockout stage of the competition since 2023, and they will have to do so this time with an inexperienced team.

articles.title: Brydon Carse will not face charges after police drop investigation into alleged assault
articles.summary: England bowler arrested after Derby night out. Cricket Regulator to decide on disciplinary action. Brydon Carse will not face any charges after Derbyshire police dropped an investigation into an alleged assault in Derby city centre last month.
body: The fast bowler was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly during a night out with his Durham teammates following a County Championship win over Derbyshire, which led to him being dropped from the England squad for their 3-0 Test series win over Pakistan.

Carse had been a non-playing member of the squad for the first Test at Headingley before being released to play for Durham, who beat Derbyshire by 338 runs to close in on promotion from Division Two, which has since been secured.

Images circulated on social media the day after the game on Sunday 23 August showed Carse in handcuffs surrounded by police officers, which led to Derbyshire police confirming a man had been arrested outside Molly Malone’s bar the following day.
“A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night,” said the police.

articles.title: Oxford United apologise for launching ‘United 93’ clothing range around 9/11 anniversary
articles.summary: ‘Campus Collection’ aimed to mark 1893 club founding. Range pulled from website two hours after launch. Oxford United have abandoned a new range of American style-sportswear after it inadvertently referenced the tragedy of September 11.
body: The League One club launched their new “Campus Collection” on Friday morning but had removed it from sale by lunchtime, after clothing designs were revealed to bear the slogan “United 93”. The U’s immediately published an apology that admitted to a lack of understanding of “the historical context and associations” related to the branding and made “sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused.”

“Inspired by the style and culture of American sports”, the club originally trailed the Campus Collection as launching on 11 September of this year, the 25th anniversary of the atrocity that killed nearly 3,000 people. Concerns over sensitivity saw the launch then delayed, but when the online collection was finally made available for sale on Friday, images showed models wearing an NFL-style shirt with “United 93” on the chest, in recognition of Oxford being founded in 1893.

articles.title: I have experienced racism a thousand times - Lamine Yamal
articles.summary: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal says he has experienced racism "a thousand times", because people are unaware their comments or behaviour are offensive.
body: The Spanish Observatory on Racism and Xenophobia, a government agency, said earlier this year that the 19-year-old and Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr were the most frequent targets of online racist abuse in Spain in the final quarter of 2025.
Lamine Yamal was among the Barca players targeted by racist abuse during El Clasico against Real Madrid at the Bernabeu in October 2024.
And in an interview with broadcaster Movistar, the winger, who helped Spain to win the World Cup in July, said he had encountered racism on a regular basis during his rise to prominence.
"A thousand times. People are indirectly racist toward you, but maybe don't realise it," he said.

articles.title: Disgraceful nothing has changed after Tarling death - Brennan
articles.summary: Britain's Matthew Brennan says it is "disgraceful that nothing has changed" in cycling to make the sport safer following the death of Fin Tarling last month.
body: Britain's Tarling, 19, died on 14 August during the Volta a Portugal following a high-speed collision with a van which had strayed on to the closed road.

Brennan, 21, who races for Dutch team Visma-Lease a Bike, told BBC Sport: "It was very sad what happened with Fin. We were watching his funeral yesterday and I said to my friend: 'It's so sad we've lost someone so special and also nothing has changed.'

"I really think that is disgraceful. Instead of someone somewhere in these organisations saying: 'OK, this should never ever happen again', it feels the world has moved on, nothing has changed and there's events where cars have been on the course still."

Six riders have died during road races in the past three years, and American rider Ezra Caudell is currently in hospital, external with "multi-system trauma" following a crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic.

articles.summary: Former Everton manager Brian Sorensen is set to join the Republic of Ireland squad for their Women's World Cup play-off qualifiers this year.
body: Sorensen is expected to take up the role of assistant coach in their set-up, alongside Liverpool's Amber Whiteley.

He will work with manager Carla Ward, who faced Sorensen's Everton in the Women's Super League when she managed Villa.
The Republic of Ireland play Kazakhstan in the first round of play-off qualifying; the two-legged tie will take place on 9 and 13 October.

articles.title: Somerset title hopes suffer major blow in Yorkshire defeat as Notts also lose
articles.summary: Somerset's hopes of becoming county champions for the first time in their history took a major blow as they collapsed to a costly defeat at the hands of Yorkshire.
body: Top of the County Championship Division One table heading into the penultimate round of matches, Somerset saw rivals Warwickshire wrap up a two-day victory against Essex but failed to keep pace at Headingley.

Chasing 287 - the highest score of the match - they were bundled out for 101 on the final day. Resuming on 73-3 they collapsed horribly as their final seven wickets fell for 25 runs in less than 13 overs.
Ben Cliff took three of them as he finished with 3-29 after taking 8-76 in the first innings, while Ben Coad claimed 4-33 and Matthew Revis 2-7.

The 185-run defeat leaves Somerset chasing from behind heading into their season-ending fixture against Surrey and one step further away from ending their 135-year quest for the county game's top prize.

articles.title: Bills get reported DJ Moore diagnosis that leaves his next game in doubt
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore left Thursday night’s 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions in the second quarter and did not return, and the reporting that followed the game pointed away from the injury Buffalo feared when he went down.
body: Ian Rapoport reported that Moore is believed to have suffered an AC joint sprain and that sources told him it is not a serious injury. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Moore’s status for next week is up in the air.

Moore was hurt with just under three minutes left in the second quarter, diving for a pass in the end zone as Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin came down on top of him. The Bills announced a shoulder injury and a stinger, listed him as questionable to return and sent him to the locker room for X-rays, then ruled him out in the third quarter, leaving him without a catch on the night.
Head coach Joe Brady said afterward that he did not have an update on the injury.
Buffalo does not play again until Sept. 27, when the Los Angeles Chargers visit at 1 p.m. ET. That leaves 10 days between the injury and the next kickoff.

articles.title: Richards looks to relaunch world championship charge against Kalajdzic
articles.summary: Craig Richards returns to his home city of London for a crucial fight when he boxes at the Copper Box Arena on September 26, live on Sky Sports.
body: Richards fights Belgrade's Radivoje Kalajdzic in the chief support to Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton.
The man from Crystal Palace is determined to beat Kalajdzic to return to world championship class.

Kalajdzic is a top-quality operator who is coming off an excellent knockout win over former WBC world champion Oleksandr Gvozdyk. He has previously boxed Artur Beterbiev and knocked out former world title challenger Sullivan Barrera too.
"I think going out there and putting on a statement performance against him puts my name in a hat for that world title, 100 per cent," Richards told Sky Sports. "I'm locked in. I'm ready to do a job.
